vision.definition: The sense that allows a person to see light, color, shape, and movement with the eyes.

pupil.definition: The opening in the center of the eye's iris that lets light in.

lens.definition: The transparent structure in the eye that helps focus light.

retina.definition: The light-sensitive layer at the back of the eye.

cornea.definition: The clear front surface of the eye.

optic-nerve.definition: The nerve carrying visual signals from the eye to the brain.

color-vision.definition: The ordinary human ability to perceive and distinguish different colors.

depth-perception.definition: The visual ability to estimate an object's distance by interpreting clues such as its apparent size, perspective, and movement.

peripheral-vision.definition: The ability to notice objects beside you without looking directly at them.

sound.definition: Something heard when vibrations reach the ears.

ear.definition: The organ used for hearing and helping maintain balance.

eardrum.definition: The membrane in the ear that vibrates to sound.
eardrum.exampleUsage: The exhibit describes the eardrum vibrating in response to sound.

cochlea.definition: A spiral-shaped structure in the inner ear that helps convert sound into nerve signals.

pitch.definition: How high or low a sound is.

volume.definition: How loud or quiet a sound is.

frequency.definition: The number of times a vibration repeats each second.

echo.definition: A sound heard again after it reflects from a surface.

vibration.definition: A rapid back-and-forth movement that can often be felt.

auditory-nerve.definition: The nerve carrying hearing signals from the inner ear to the brain.

nose.definition: The organ of smell and entrance to the respiratory tract.

nostril.definition: Either one of the two external openings to the nasal cavity in the nose.

olfactory.definition: Relating to the sense of smell.

aroma.definition: A noticeable smell, often a pleasant one from food or drink.

odor.definition: A smell, especially one that is noticeable.

scent.definition: A distinctive smell, including one used by animals to recognize or follow something.

stench.definition: A distinctive odor that is offensively unpleasant.

pungent.definition: Having a very strong and sharp smell or taste.

nasal-cavity.definition: Either of the two hollow passages inside the nose, located above the mouth and extending back to the throat.

tongue.definition: The muscular part inside the mouth used in tasting, speaking, and swallowing.

taste-bud.definition: A small group of sensory cells that helps detect taste, mainly on the tongue.

sweet.definition: Having or denoting the characteristic taste of sugar.

sour.definition: Having an acidic taste like lemon or vinegar.

salty.definition: Tasting of salt or containing a lot of salt.

bitter.definition: Causing a sharp and acrid taste experience.

umami.definition: A savory taste found in foods such as mushrooms and aged cheese.

flavor.definition: The combined taste and smell experienced when eating or drinking.

palate.definition: The upper surface of the mouth that separates the oral and nasal cavities.

savor.definition: To notice and enjoy a taste or flavor slowly.

skin.definition: A natural protective body covering and site of the sense of touch.

nerve-ending.definition: A tiny end branch of a nerve that helps send sensory information between body tissues and the nervous system.
nerve-ending.exampleUsage: Nerve endings in the skin help us notice touch and temperature.

pressure.definition: The somatic sensation that results from applying force to an area of skin.

temperature.definition: How hot or cold something is.

texture.definition: The way a surface looks or feels.

pain.definition: An unpleasant feeling caused by injury or illness.

tickle.definition: A feeling caused by light touches that may make someone laugh.

itch.definition: An uncomfortable skin sensation that makes you want to scratch.

smooth.definition: Having a surface free from roughness or bumps or ridges or irregularities.

rough.definition: Having or caused by an irregular surface.

bright.definition: Giving off or reflecting a lot of light.

loud.definition: Characterized by or producing sound of great volume or intensity.

fragrant.definition: Having a pleasant and noticeable smell.

soft.definition: Easy to press or bend, and not hard to the touch.

dark.definition: Having little or no light in the sense taught here.

bland.definition: Lacking taste or flavor or tang.

hard.definition: Firm and difficult to press, bend, or cut.
